rules: 1. An application with its own frontend and backend code in the repo (not a library, framework, or SDK), public, not archived.

2. Its default branch has a commit before the window opens (startSha: the last one before 2026-07-01T00:00:00Z) and after it (endSha: the last one before 2026-10-31T00:00:00Z, when the follow-up ends), endSha descending from startSha (GitHub's compare says `ahead`).

3. At least 20 PRs merged into the default branch in the window, per GitHub's search (`is:pr is:merged base:<branch> merged:2026-07-01..2026-09-30`) on the day of pinning. A busier repo is kept; only its first maxPrsPerRepo by merge time are replayed.
4. The analyzer (built at 22327d2, analyzer code last changed in 6e15308) finishes on startSha within its limits (20,000 source files, 50 MB of source).

5. At least 20 `http` edges reach a route from app code at startSha (measured.appHttpToRoute: call sites outside test packages, test folders, and *.test.* / *.spec.* files), since only an edge that reaches a route can break.
candidates: A hand-made list of 35 known open-source apps in the supported stack (React/Next.js frontends, Express or Next API routes), plus every result with at least 20 PRs merged in the window (rule 3's search) from three GitHub repository searches sorted by stars, up to 50 results each: `topic:express topic:react stars:>200 pushed:>2026-10-01` (12 results), `topic:nextjs topic:prisma stars:>1000 pushed:>2026-10-01` (12), `topic:nodejs topic:react stars:>1000 pushed:>2026-10-01` (44). Every candidate is pinned or listed under `rejected` with the first rule it fails, checked in order. Rule 1 is a reading of each repo's description and layout; rules 2 to 5 were measured by scripts. No PR was replayed before pinning.

repos.name: cal.diy
repos.why: Cal.com's monorepo (renamed from calcom/cal.com): the Next.js app `@calcom/web` and app-store packages call `@calcom/web`'s Next API routes (35 of 39 edges); most of its client-server traffic is tRPC, which isn't analyzed.

repos.name: dub.link
repos.why: Dub (renamed from dubinc/dub): the Next.js app `web` calls its own Next API routes with fetch and SWR (399 edges), plus 3 from the shared `@dub/ui` package.

repos.name: maxun
repos.why: One package: a React frontend calling the Express server in the same package with axios (72 edges).

repos.name: Claude-Code-Agent-Monitor
repos.why: A React client package (`agent-dashboard-client`) calling a separate Express server package (`agent-dashboard`, 80 edges).

repos.name: anything-llm
repos.why: A React (Vite) frontend calling two Express services: the server (206 edges) and the document collector (113), plus 11 between the services themselves.

repos.name: seerr
repos.why: Seerr (Jellyseerr's successor, renamed from fallenbagel/jellyseerr): one package whose Next.js frontend calls the Express API under `/api/v1` in the same package with axios and SWR (300 edges).

repos.name: comp
repos.why: Two Next.js apps (`@trycompai/app`, `@trycompai/portal`) calling their own and each other's Next API routes (39 edges, plus 1 from `@trycompai/framework-editor`); their requests to the NestJS API (`apps/api`) stay unresolved, since NestJS isn't supported.
